Project Mandela 1.2.0

Released 2026-10-29 · GitHub release · CHANGELOG.md

1.2.0 — 2026-10-29 — Gradle / JDK 21 modernization

Added

  • A deck starter template in EditorServices.starterTemplates(): a console-safe program that assembles a small Presentoire slide deck as Markdown in a list and prints it, so Espresso's new *Presentoire Deck* action can drop a runnable deck skeleton into an empty buffer. It prints rather than writes, because the language depends on nothing and Espresso runs the console profile; scripts/mandela/deck-new.mnd is the sandboxed generator that writes the .md file. The grammar is untouched, so mandela.language stays 1.0 and no version copy moves.
  • Str.between(open, close) — the text strictly between the first open and the first close after it, or null when either delimiter is absent. It is the indexOf-pair-and-substring span every scanner in scripts/mandela/ hand-rolls (a changelog header's [version], a bold **title**, a link's label and target), stated once as a member. Delimiters are literal, never a pattern, so the no-regex limit (§12 of the guide) is unchanged; null on a miss is the same not-found List.find answers, which keeps an empty span distinguishable from no match. A member addition, so mandela.language stays 1.0 and no existing script changes behaviour.
  • A guard on for — for x in xs if pred { … } visits only the elements whose guard is truthy and skips the rest, the loop-and-filter idiom the gates in scripts/mandela/ otherwise write as a filter before the loop or an if around the whole body. The guard reads the loop variable and belongs to the header's own line, so a body that *opens* with an if statement is still a statement and never a guard — pinned from both sides in SyntaxTest and IterationTest, with two scenarios in the Cucumber language_semantics feature. This is new syntax a script can observe, so it moves the language axis: mandela.language goes 1.0 → 1.1 and the three copies the gate compares (gradle.properties, Mandela.LANGUAGE_VERSION, the guide line) agree. The jar axis stays 1.1.0 and moves only when a release is cut. ROADMAP §3.2's first candidate, shipped.
  • Str.format(fields) — "{name}:{port}".format({"name": "host", "port": 8080}) assembles a line from named fields, the report every gate in scripts/mandela/ otherwise builds with padEnd and +. Each {field} is replaced by the display of its value — the same rendering println and ${…} use, so a string arrives bare and a number as written — {{ and }} are the literal braces, and a field the map does not carry raises a ValueError naming it rather than dropping the column silently. There is no positional form and no format spec. A member addition, so it rides the jar axis and leaves mandela.language at 1.1; ROADMAP §3.2's third candidate, shipped.
  • Capabilities.probe(root) — a fifth sandbox profile for a CI probe: the desktop(root) shape (console, files under one root, a thread) plus read-only ENV, so a probe may read a build's own variables while it asserts what must hold about the tree. ENV is the only widening over desktop, and it is read-only by nature — there is no grant to write an environment variable — so a probe still gets no JVM type, no socket and no child process. A Capabilities change, so no grammar moves under it and mandela.language stays 1.1; ROADMAP §3.2's fourth candidate, shipped.
  • match type arms, documented — the machine already dispatched on a value's type (is Int, n is Int, and the Point(x, y) record destructure) beside the literal, guard, list and _ arms, but the language guide's Match section never said so. §5 now documents the type arm as the same is the expression form uses, pinned by a LanguageTest case and a Cucumber scenario. No behaviour changes and no axis moves: this closes the gap between the grammar and its guide, ROADMAP §3.2's second candidate.

Fixed

  • The Pages portal now reaches every guide, and a dead link on the published release archive is gone. documentation/index.html surfaced only the language and embedding guides; it now cards the whole docs/ set (README, architecture, functional analysis, development, usage, roadmap, history) plus AGENTS.md, each at its GitHub blob URL — the site stays a static copy with no renderer, so a card opens the same Markdown a reader of the repository sees. Separately, whats-new.mnd built a blob href by naive concatenation, so the stale ../gradle.properties link in the [1.0.0] entry rendered as …/blob/main/../gradle.properties — a GitHub 404 on the live page that htmlLinksCheck cannot see (it skips absolute https:// refs). The generator now resolves each changelog target against the repository root and clamps any .. that would escape it, the same way doc-links.mnd does; the archive was re-rendered and whatsNewCheck is green. Docs and CI only — no grammar, no version axis moves.

The test reports of a published release are generated beside this page: <version>/reports/ carries the JUnit, JaCoCo, Cucumber and PIT mutation reports of every module with a test suite. Each module runs report-only (mutationThreshold = 0, no gate) unless it appears in the mutationExemptions map, where it is gated at the score its own suite really achieves. The same tree is attached to the GitHub release as reports-<version>.zip, so a report outlives a rebuilt site.
